definitions.explanation: Marks the group or population that an action, survey, service, or rule is directed at. The noun before を is the target audience.

examples.japanese: {学生|がくせい}を{対象|たいしょう}にした{調査|ちょうさ}。
{子|こ}どもを{対象|たいしょう}に{英語|えいご}{教室|きょうしつ}を{開|ひら}く。
examples.english: To open an English class aimed at children.

examples.japanese: この{割引|わりびき}は{初|はじ}めて{利用|りよう}するお{客様|きゃくさま}を{対象|たいしょう}にしています。
examples.english: This discount is intended for customers using the service for the first time.

notes:
Often appears as {対象|たいしょう}にした or {対象|たいしょう}にして modifying a following noun. The fuller form is を{対象|たいしょう}にして; を{対象|たいしょう}に is the common shortened version.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ...を{対象|たいしょう}にした{調査|ちょうさ}: a survey targeting ...
- ...を{対象|たいしょう}にして{行|おこな}う: to carry out aimed at ...
- {全社員|ぜんしゃいん}を{対象|たいしょう}に: targeting all employees

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {向|む}け: aimed at — attaches directly to a noun ({子|こ}ども{向|む}け); more casual
- を{中心|ちゅうしん}に: centered on — emphasizes the focal point rather than the target group
